location: p. r9, General Discussion (see also p. r3, Experiment 1, Results)
quote: In the ﬁrst experiment, the similarity effect was replicated,
reason: The target effect is the main effect of phonemic similarity on the number of sequences recalled in Experiment 1. In Experiment 1, the replication found a significant main effect of phonemic similarity (F(1, 28) = 57.30, p < .001, eta_p^2 = .67) and explicitly stated in the General Discussion that the similarity effect was replicated in the first experiment. Shipped erroneously coded 'failed' (which applies to articulatory suppression, not phonemic similarity).

The target effect is the main effect of presentation rate on correctly recalled items in Experiment 4 (Longoni et al., 1993, p. 17: F(1, 20) = 31.04). In the replication's Experiment 4 Results (p. r7), the main effect of presentation rate (factor D) is F(1, 20) = 0.072, p = .79. Shipped extracted F(1, 20) = 1.048, which is the interaction between phonemic similarity and presentation rate (B x D).
